name: Tor (C tor daemon, Tor Expert Bundle)
purpose: Reference C implementation of the Tor anonymity network (client, onion-service host and relay). On Windows the Tor Project ships it as the Tor Expert Bundle (tor.exe, pluggable transports, GeoIP data), which BTCortex runs per user as the SOCKS proxy and onion-service host for Bitcoin Core, Electrum servers, Lightning nodes and wallets.

maintenance.evidence: tor 0.4.9.14 was released on 2026-10-07 as a security release ('Another week, another security release'; fixes tracked as TROVE-2026-062 and TROVE-2026-067 among others). The 0.4.9 series became stable on 2026-02-12, 0.4.8 reached end of life on 2026-06-01 and the 0.5.0 merge window opened on 2026-03-25 (CoreTorReleases wiki). Tor Expert Bundle 15.0.25 (tor 0.4.9.14) was published on dist.torproject.org on 2026-10-12 together with Tor Browser 15.0.25.

platforms.windowsVersions: Not stated for the Expert Bundle. Tor Browser dropped Windows 7, 8 and 8.1 with Tor Browser 14 and the Tor Project recommends Windows 10 or 11.
platforms.windowsDistribution: Tor Expert Bundle tar.gz archives without an installer: tor-expert-bundle-windows-x86_64-<Tor Browser version>.tar.gz and tor-expert-bundle-windows-i686-<version>.tar.gz, each with a detached OpenPGP signature (.asc) made with the Tor Browser Developers signing key, plus a signed sha256sums-signed-build.txt. tor.exe in 15.0.25 has no Authenticode signature (empty PE certificate table). No Windows ARM64 build. The Tor Project states that Tor Browser 16.0 drops 32-bit x86 platforms.
platforms.other: Expert Bundles for Linux (x86_64, i686; aarch64 only in the 16.0 alpha), macOS (x86_64, aarch64) and Android; source tarball for Unix-like systems; distribution packages.

interfaces.description: SOCKS4/4a/5 listener (SocksPort, default 9050; BTCortex binds 127.0.0.1 only). Separate SocksPort lines are isolated from each other by default, and IsolateSOCKSAuth (on by default) puts streams with different SOCKS5 username/password on different circuits, which Bitcoin Core's proxyrandomize uses. Tor's SOCKS extensions add RESOLVE/RESOLVE_PTR and extended onion-service error codes.
interfaces.authentication: None (loopback only). SOCKS5 username/password is used for stream isolation, not access control.

interfaces.description: Tor control protocol on ControlPort over TCP (ControlSocket Unix sockets are not available on Windows). Line-based with SMTP-style reply codes (250 OK, 514 authentication required, 515 bad authentication, 552 unrecognised entity, 650 asynchronous event). BTCortex uses PROTOCOLINFO, AUTHCHALLENGE, AUTHENTICATE, GETINFO (version, status/bootstrap-phase, status/circuit-established, status/enough-dir-info, network-liveness, net/listeners/socks, onions/current, status/version/current), SETEVENTS (STATUS_CLIENT, STATUS_GENERAL, HS_DESC, NETWORK_LIVENESS), ADD_ONION, DEL_ONION, SIGNAL (SHUTDOWN, HALT, NEWNYM, RELOAD) and TAKEOWNERSHIP.
interfaces.authentication: SAFECOOKIE (HMAC-SHA256 challenge-response over the 32-byte control_auth_cookie; recommended), COOKIE (deprecated by the specification), HASHEDPASSWORD (HashedControlPassword) or NULL (must never be used).

interfaces.description: tor.exe -f <torrc>, --defaults-torrc <file>, --verify-config, --dump-config short|full, --hash-password <password>, --version, --list-modules and --service install|remove|start|stop (administrator only). Any torrc option can also be given on the command line ('--SocksPort 9050' or 'SocksPort 9050'); a '+' prefix appends to and a '/' prefix removes options from the configuration file.

torrc and a defaults file; DataDirectory (state, cached consensus and microdescriptors, lock, control_auth_cookie); one HiddenServiceDir per onion service containing hostname, hs_ed25519_secret_key, hs_ed25519_public_key and authorized_clients/*.auth; ClientOnionAuthDir containing <name>.auth_private files; log files.
interfaces.authentication: NTFS permissions of the per-user directories

interfaces.description: Optional MetricsPort answering HTTP GET /metrics in Prometheus format. MetricsPortPolicy must be set (reject-all by default). The manual warns that exposing metrics publicly endangers Tor users; keep it on loopback if it is enabled at all.

cli: tor.exe -f <torrc> --defaults-torrc <defaults> __OwningControllerProcess <pid>; tor.exe --verify-config -f <torrc>; tor.exe --hash-password <password> (for HashedControlPassword); tor.exe --version. tor --service install [--options ...] creates the Windows service 'tor' (display name 'Tor Win32 Service', auto-start, account NT AUTHORITY\LocalService) and needs administrator rights, as do --service start|stop|remove.
remoteManagement: Only through the control protocol. The ControlPort grants full control (configuration, onion-service keys, shutdown) and must never leave loopback; tor instances on remote machines or node platforms can be monitored through an SSH tunnel to their ControlPort with that machine's own authentication.
nodeCompatibility: Bitcoin Core: proxy=127.0.0.1:9050 (or proxy=<addr>=tor / onion=<addr> for onion-only routing; DNS lookups only use the generic or IPv4/IPv6 proxy), torcontrol=127.0.0.1:9051 with SAFECOOKIE (Core reads COOKIEFILE from PROTOCOLINFO, so it must run as the same Windows user) or torpassword with HashedControlPassword; when listening, Core creates an ephemeral v3 onion service with ADD_ONION and stores its key in onion_v3_private_key; onlynet=onion (the alias 'tor' was removed in 31.0); privatebroadcast (31.0+, use 31.1 or later); 32.0 enables proof-of-work defences for its onion service. Fulcrum: tor_proxy (default 127.0.0.1:9050) for .onion peer discovery, tor_hostname and tor_*_port to announce an onion endpoint, inbound via HiddenServicePort. Sparrow: useProxy/proxyServer or its internal Tor. Electrum: proxy socks5:127.0.0.1:9050. Wasabi bundles its own tor on 37150/37151.

dependencies.notes: Pluggable transports (obfs4, Snowflake, WebTunnel, meek) for bridges; lyrebird.exe ships in the Expert Bundle.
Experimental Conjure transport; conjure-client.exe ships in the Expert Bundle.

networking: Outbound TCP to guard relays, fallback directories or bridges (any port). No inbound port is needed for client use or for onion services, which work behind NAT and firewalls. Local listeners: SocksPort 9050 and ControlPort 9051 by default (Tor Browser uses 9150/9151, Wasabi's bundled tor 37150/37151); BTCortex binds both to 127.0.0.1 and checks for conflicts first. DisableNetwork 1 allows a configured but offline start. Bootstrap requires a correct system clock (CLOCK_SKEW status event).
storage: Expert Bundle 15.0.25 for Windows x86_64: 21 MB archive; tor.exe 10.2 MB, tor-gencert.exe 6.2 MB, lyrebird.exe 18.0 MB, conjure-client.exe 13.1 MB, geoip 9.8 MB and geoip6 16.6 MB extracted (measured from the archive listing on 2026-10-21). The DataDirectory caches the consensus and microdescriptors; its size was not measured.
resources: No official RAM or CPU figures for a client; not measured on the test machine.
security: Verify the archive's OpenPGP signature against the Tor Browser Developers key (primary fingerprint EF6E 286D DA85 EA2A 4BA7 DE68 4E2C 6E87 9329 8290; 15.0.25 was signed with subkey 022D A248 432D 2A0E 0F54 E65E 316C 1FAC D62D 07D9) and the SHA-256 in the signed sha256sums-signed-build.txt; Authenticode cannot be used because tor.exe is unsigned. Releases are frequent and often security-relevant (0.4.9.14 fixed several high-severity bugs), so the update channel matters. The ControlPort is equivalent to full control of tor and its onion-service keys; use SAFECOOKIE, keep the DataDirectory and cookie readable only by the user (HiddenServiceDirGroupReadable has no effect on Windows) and never expose SocksPort or ControlPort beyond loopback (the manual warns that a non-local SocksPort leaks traffic and creates an open proxy). hs_ed25519_secret_key is the onion identity and must be protected and backed up like a credential. Log at notice level or below (the manual warns that more verbose logs may provide sensitive information). Tor does not start from paths containing non-ASCII characters (issue #10416 open; the proposed fix MR !357 was closed unmerged). A Tor-only node is exposed to Sybil and eclipse risks on a smaller address set.
licenceNotes: The Expert Bundle also contains libevent, OpenSSL, zlib, lyrebird and Conjure under their own licences (docs/*.txt in the archive). Redistribution of the unmodified bundle is permitted; 'Tor' and the onion logo are trademarks of The Tor Project, whose trademark guidelines were not reviewed here.
integrationMechanisms: Resolve the current stable version (download.torproject.org/tor/ or the Tor Browser downloads.json) and download the Expert Bundle for the machine's architecture from dist.torproject.org (archive.torproject.org/tor-package-archive as fallback)

Verify the detached .asc against a pinned Tor Browser Developers key with OpenPGP.js, cross-check the SHA-256 in the signed sha256sums-signed-build.txt, then extract with path validation to %LOCALAPPDATA%\BTCortex\runtimes\tor\<version>
Generate torrc and an explicit defaults file; launch tor.exe as a per-user child process with __OwningControllerProcess, then TAKEOWNERSHIP over an authenticated control connection
Authenticate with SAFECOOKIE, subscribe to STATUS_CLIENT, STATUS_GENERAL, HS_DESC and NETWORK_LIVENESS events and track bootstrap through status/bootstrap-phase
Create onion services with HiddenServiceDir/HiddenServicePort or ADD_ONION (Detach, PoWDefensesEnabled) and display hostnames; monitor HS_DESC UPLOADED events
Write bitcoin.conf (proxy, torcontrol, onlynet), Fulcrum, Sparrow, Electrum and Lightning proxy settings that point at dedicated SocksPorts
Detect external tor installations (listening 9050/9051, 9150/9151, 37150/37151; tor.exe processes; Windows service 'tor') with PROTOCOLINFO probes only
Stop with SIGNAL SHUTDOWN and wait, falling back to SIGNAL HALT and then process termination

feasibility.notes: Official signed Windows archive, no installer and no administrator rights, a complete documented control protocol and a reference launcher (Tor Browser's tor-launcher) to copy. Open work: non-ASCII profile paths, port conflicts with other tor instances, antivirus or application-control policies against unsigned executables in user-writable folders, and bridges for censored networks.

notes: The Expert Bundle version number follows Tor Browser (15.0.25 contains tor 0.4.9.14); its data/torrc-defaults is Tor Browser's file and refers to TorBrowser\Tor\PluggableTransports paths that do not exist in the bundle, so BTCortex must write its own ClientTransportPlugin lines. Arti (arti) is the long-term successor but cannot yet replace C tor for BTCortex (no official binaries, no control port, onion-service hosting still documented as experimental). Do not depend on Tor Browser's tor (tor-browser).

name: Tor Browser
purpose: Hardened Firefox ESR-based browser bundled with its own tor process, for browsing the web and onion services anonymously. Useful to BTCortex users for opening onion block explorers and web interfaces, but it is not a general-purpose managed Tor daemon.

maintenance.evidence: Tor Browser 15.0.25 published 2026-10-12 (Firefox ESR security updates, tor 0.4.9.14, OpenSSL 3.5.9); 15.0 was released on 2025-10-28 on Firefox ESR 140; 16.0 is in alpha (16.0a14 directory dated 2026-10-16).

platforms.windowsVersions: Windows 10 or 11 recommended; support for Windows 7, 8 and 8.1 ended with Tor Browser 14 and the 13.5 legacy line ended with 13.5.29 in March 2026.
platforms.windowsDistribution: tor-browser-windows-x86_64-portable-15.0.25.exe and tor-browser-windows-i686-portable-15.0.25.exe (per-user portable installers) with detached .asc signatures by the Tor Browser Developers key; incremental and full .mar updates. Tor Browser 16.0 drops 32-bit x86.
platforms.other: Linux (x86_64, i686), macOS, Android.

interfaces.description: Browser user interface with connection assistance and bridge settings.
The bundled tor listens on 127.0.0.1:9150 (default of the tor-launcher code) with flags 'ExtendedErrors IPv6Traffic PreferIPv6 KeepAliveIsolateSOCKSAuth', only while the browser is running.
ControlPort 9151 (preference extensions.torlauncher.control_port) with cookie authentication; the browser owns the process through __OwningControllerProcess.
interfaces.authentication: Cookie authentication; the cookie file lives in the browser's data directory

cli: firefox.exe from the Tor Browser folder; launching with a URL argument opens it in Tor Browser. Environment variables such as TOR_SKIP_LAUNCH and TOR_SOCKS_PORT change how it starts tor (documented in Arti's README for use with Arti).
nodeCompatibility: None directly. Bitcoin Core's tor.md notes that Tor Browser's proxy listens on 9150; using it for a node only works while the browser is open.
networking: Outbound Tor connections from its bundled tor; local SOCKS 9150 and control 9151 on loopback while running.
resources: Similar to Firefox ESR; not measured.
security: Downloads are signed with the same Tor Browser Developers key as the Expert Bundle. Tor Browser updates itself, changes its tor version without notice to other programs, and its tor exits when the browser closes, so services that depend on it break and onion services disappear. Routing other applications through Tor Browser's SOCKS port mixes their circuits with browsing. BTCortex must only launch it (for example to open an onion explorer URL) and must never read its cookie or control its tor.
licenceNotes: Based on Firefox ESR (MPL-2.0) with additional components under their own licences; Tor Project trademarks apply.
integrationMechanisms: Detect an installation (default per-user folder 'Tor Browser' on the desktop or chosen path) and the running tor on 9150/9151
Launch firefox.exe with an onion URL chosen by the user, for example a local block explorer's onion address
Warn when an application is configured to use 9150 instead of BTCortex's managed tor

feasibility.notes: Launching is simple; managing it as a daemon is inappropriate by design.

notes: Tor Browser's launcher is the reference for how a controller should start tor: '-f torrc', DataDirectory, ClientOnionAuthDir, '--defaults-torrc', GeoIPFile and GeoIPv6File next to torrc-defaults, '+__ControlPort', CookieAuthentication 1 with an explicit CookieAuthFile, '+__SocksPort' and '__OwningControllerProcess <pid>', with DisableNetwork 1 while the network settings are shown.

name: Arti
purpose: The Tor Project's Rust reimplementation of Tor, designed as an embeddable library (arti-client) and a SOCKS proxy binary; intended long-term successor of C tor.

maintenance.evidence: Monthly releases: 2.7.0 on 2026-10-01, 2.6.0 on 2026-09-01, 2.5.1 on 2026-08-03 (tags arti-v2.7.0 etc.). 2.7.0 contained several low- and medium-severity security fixes. The README (status as of August 2026) says work is focused on relay and directory-authority support.

platforms.windowsDistribution: No official binaries ('We expect to be providing official binaries soon'); build from source with 'cargo build -p arti --locked --release' (MSRV Rust 1.92). The support policy lists Windows as a target with automated builds but no automated tests.
platforms.other: Linux (target, tested), macOS and iOS (targets), Android.

interfaces.description: SOCKS proxy started with 'arti proxy', default port 9150; supports Tor's SOCKS extensions and HTTP CONNECT extensions.
Arti RPC (JSON-based, declared stable in 1.4.2 on 2025-03-31; 'rpc' feature in the 'full' feature set). It is not compatible with C tor's control protocol.
arti-client Rust crate for embedding Tor connections in applications.

cli: arti proxy [-p <socks port>] [-c <config>]; configuration file on Windows: %APPDATA%\torproject\Arti\config\arti.toml. Onion-service hosting needs a build with the 'onion-service-service' feature, which is not in the default feature set.
nodeCompatibility: Can serve as a SOCKS proxy for Bitcoin Core's outbound connections and for wallets. Bitcoin Core's automatic onion service (and any tool that uses ADD_ONION, GETINFO or SETEVENTS) needs C tor's control port, which Arti does not implement.
networking: Outbound Tor connections; local SOCKS port 9150 by default (same as Tor Browser).
security: Rust memory safety removes a class of bugs. Arti's own onion-service document at tag arti-v2.7.0 still says hosting is 'suitable for testing and experimentation only' and 'may even compromise the privacy of your other uses of the same Arti instance', while the README and Compatibility.md (February 2026) say Arti supports running onion services; BTCortex must treat hosting as not production-ready. The arti.torproject.org limitations page is marked as not updated since 2023.
licenceNotes: The equix and hashx crates (onion-service proof-of-work) are LGPL-3.0; the project documents the implications for binary redistribution in doc/LGPL-and-rust.md.
integrationMechanisms: Track releases and official-binary availability
Allow the user to point applications at an existing Arti SOCKS port as a connected application, with the limitation that onion services and control-port features are unavailable

feasibility.notes: No official Windows binaries, no C-tor control protocol and onion-service hosting not yet production-ready; BTCortex would have to build and ship Arti itself. Re-evaluate when official binaries exist and hosting is declared stable.

notes: Compatibility.md: 'Going forward, Arti is the preferred Tor client for new feature development.' Recommendation for BTCortex today: C tor from the Expert Bundle.

sources.title: arti crate README (features, Windows configuration path)

unverifiedClaims: The Arti RPC method set (for example whether it can create onion services or report bootstrap state) was not reviewed.
No Windows build of Arti was attempted.

name: lyrebird (Tor pluggable transports)
purpose: The Tor Project's pluggable-transport binary (fork of obfs4proxy) implementing obfs4, meek_lite, WebTunnel, Snowflake (since 0.5.0) and the legacy obfs2, obfs3 and ScrambleSuit transports, used by tor to reach bridges on censored networks.

maintenance.evidence: 0.9.0 on 2026-09-21 (goreleaser packages, Snowflake proxy fix); 0.8.1 on 2026-01-14; 0.7.0 on 2025-11-19 (WebTunnel certificate pinning, uTLS by default).

platforms.windowsDistribution: lyrebird.exe inside the Tor Expert Bundle (tor\pluggable_transports\), covered by the bundle's signature.
platforms.other: Linux, macOS, Android (in the respective Expert Bundles).

interfaces.description: Pluggable Transport protocol v1 child process launched by tor through 'ClientTransportPlugin <transports> exec <path>\lyrebird.exe'.

networking: Outbound only, to bridges, domain fronts (meek, Snowflake broker) or WebRTC peers (Snowflake, STUN servers listed in the bridge lines).
security: Bridges hide the fact of Tor use from a local observer but do not add anonymity; built-in bridge lines are public and may be blocked. Snowflake and meek depend on third-party CDNs and domain fronting.
integrationMechanisms: Generate ClientTransportPlugin lines with absolute paths from pt_config.json in the bundle
Offer built-in obfs4, Snowflake and meek bridge lines from pt_config.json and user-supplied bridge lines (for example WebTunnel from BridgeDB)

feasibility.notes: Shipped and verified with tor; only configuration is needed.

notes: The version of lyrebird inside Expert Bundle 15.0.25 was not determined.

unverifiedClaims: The lyrebird version bundled in 15.0.25 was not read from the binary.

name: Conjure pluggable transport (conjure-client)
purpose: Refraction-networking (decoy routing) pluggable transport that reaches a Tor bridge through phantom addresses in deploying ISPs' unused address space.

maintenance.evidence: Repository last activity 2026-09-01 (GitLab API); no tags. conjure-client.exe ships in Expert Bundle 15.0.25.

platforms.windowsDistribution: conjure-client.exe inside the Tor Expert Bundle.

interfaces.description: Pluggable transport launched by tor: 'ClientTransportPlugin conjure exec conjure-client.exe -registerURL https://registration.refraction.network/api'.

networking: Registration over HTTPS to registration.refraction.network, then connections to phantom proxies.
security: The bundled README warns: 'This tool and the deployment is still under active development' and 'Do not expect this to work out of the box in all areas'; the station is sometimes overloaded.
licenceNotes: Licence text ships as docs/conjure.txt in the Expert Bundle; not read.
integrationMechanisms: Offer as an experimental bridge option only

feasibility.notes: Technically configurable like other transports, but upstream describes it as experimental and capacity-limited.

name: obfs4proxy (Yawning Angel)
purpose: Original obfs4 pluggable-transport proxy, forked and renamed lyrebird by the Tor Project.

maintenance.evidence: Last tag obfs4proxy-0.0.14 on 2022-09-04; repository last active 2024-12-11 (GitLab API). The Expert Bundle ships lyrebird.exe instead of obfs4proxy.exe.

integrationMechanisms: Detect obfs4proxy.exe references in imported torrc files and rewrite them to the bundled lyrebird.exe

feasibility.notes: Superseded by lyrebird, which ships with the Expert Bundle.

name: i2pd (I2P daemon)
purpose: Lightweight C++ router for the I2P anonymity network. It enables the SAM bridge by default, which Bitcoin Core uses through -i2psam to make and accept I2P peer connections.

maintenance.evidence: 3.0.0 released 2026-10-20 (full SAM 3.3, I2PControl LocalDestinationInfo, keys files readable by owner only); 2.61.0 on 2026-07-20; 2.60.0 on 2026-04-25. Default branch 'openssl' pushed 2026-10-20.

platforms.windowsVersions: A separate Windows XP-compatible build is offered; the minimum for the main builds is not stated.
platforms.windowsDistribution: i2pd_<version>_win64_mingw.zip, i2pd_<version>_win32_mingw.zip, i2pd_<version>_winxp_mingw.zip and setup_i2pd_v<version>.exe on GitHub Releases. Release builds are Win32 tray applications. 2.61.0 has SHA512SUMS and SHA512SUMS.asc (issuer 9519 28BB 3170 24EF D053 D73C 66F6 C87B 98EB CFE2, R4SAS); the 3.0.0 release had no SHA512SUMS or signature on 2026-10-21.
platforms.other: Linux (deb, rpm for many distributions), macOS, Android, FreeBSD and others.

interfaces.description: SAM application bridge (sam.enabled true by default, usually 127.0.0.1:7656; SAM UDP 7655). Bitcoin Core speaks SAM 3.1 to it.
Web console (http.enabled true, port 7070) and HTTP proxy (httpproxy, port 4444); both enabled by default.
interfaces.authentication: Optional HTTP basic authentication for the web console

interfaces.description: SOCKS proxy into I2P (socksproxy, port 4447, enabled by default).
I2PControl JSON-RPC over HTTPS (i2pcontrol.enabled false by default, port 7650): Authenticate, RouterInfo, RouterManager (Shutdown, ShutdownGraceful), plus the i2pd-specific LocalDestinationInfo.
interfaces.authentication: Password (default 'itoopie', must be changed) exchanged for a session token; self-signed TLS certificate i2pcontrol.crt.pem

interfaces.description: i2pd.conf (INI) and tunnels.conf in the data directory; router keys, netDb and peer profiles.

cli: i2pd.exe --datadir=<dir> --conf=<dir>\i2pd.conf --tunconf=<dir>\tunnels.conf [--service] [--loglevel=warn]. datadir and service are command-line-only options. Without --datadir the data directory is the executable's folder if it contains i2pd.conf, otherwise %APPDATA%\i2pd; --service uses C:\ProgramData\i2pd. The 'daemon' option defaults to false in the source (Config.cpp) although the documentation table says true.
remoteManagement: I2PControl JSON-RPC (HTTPS, password) and the web console; both should stay on loopback.
nodeCompatibility: Bitcoin Core (22.0+): i2psam=127.0.0.1:7656, i2pacceptincoming=1 (default; a persistent I2P address with its key in i2p_private_key in the data directory) or 0 (transient address per outbound connection), onlynet=i2p optional. Core uses SAM 3.1, so it listens and advertises with port 0 and only connects to I2P addresses with port 0. Core's I2P documentation recommends i2pd as the lighter alternative.
networking: NTCP2 and SSU2 transports on a random port (port option, default 'auto') on all interfaces; UPnP is false by default for the command-line build but true for the GUI builds (Windows, Android). Participates in transit tunnels by default, which Core's documentation asks users not to restrict. Local listeners: 7070 web console, 4444 HTTP proxy, 4447 SOCKS proxy, 7656 SAM, 7654 I2CP (enabled by default), 7650 I2PControl (disabled by default).
storage: Windows x64 ZIP 4.9 MB (3.0.0); netDb and profiles are small.
resources: Bandwidth limit configurable (bandwidth L=32 KB/s, O=256 KB/s, P=2048 KB/s, X=unlimited; share percentage for transit); RAM and CPU not measured.
security: Unlike Tor, the receiver of an I2P connection sees the initiator's I2P address (Core's i2p.md), so transient addresses (i2pacceptincoming=0) are preferable when inbound is not needed. Disable UPnP for BTCortex-managed routers (Windows GUI builds enable it by default) and bind every local service to 127.0.0.1. Change the default I2PControl password. A non-administrator user who sees the Windows Firewall prompt for i2pd's transport listener gets block rules whatever they choose; I2P still works outbound but is reachability-limited. Verify the 2.61.0-style SHA512SUMS.asc when present; for 3.0.0 no signature was published at the time of checking.
integrationMechanisms: Download the win64 ZIP, verify SHA512SUMS and its OpenPGP signature (R4SAS key), extract per user

Generate i2pd.conf (SAM on 127.0.0.1:7656, web console on 127.0.0.1 with authentication or disabled, HTTP and SOCKS proxies disabled unless needed, upnp disabled, I2PControl on 127.0.0.1 with a random password) and launch with --datadir and --conf
Health: SAM 'HELLO VERSION' handshake on 7656 and I2PControl RouterInfo; Bitcoin Core getnetworkinfo shows the i2p network as reachable
Stop through I2PControl RouterManager Shutdown (immediate) or ShutdownGraceful (finishes transit tunnels, up to about ten minutes)
Write bitcoin.conf i2psam and i2pacceptincoming settings

feasibility.notes: Portable signed ZIP and simple INI configuration, but the Windows builds are tray applications, the newest release lacked checksums at the time of checking, UPnP is on by default in the GUI build, and the transport listener triggers a Windows Firewall prompt.

notes: I2P's SAM v3 specification page (updated 2026-07) says i2pd did not support most SAM 3.2/3.3 features; i2pd 3.0.0 (2026-10-20) announces a full SAM 3.3 implementation. Bitcoin Core only needs SAM 3.1.
unverifiedClaims: The signing key fingerprint was taken from the signature packet and matched on keys.openpgp.org; no fingerprint was found on i2pd's own pages.
Whether SHA512SUMS and a signature will be added to the 3.0.0 release later was not known on 2026-10-21.
The minimum Windows version of the main builds and the bind address defaults of the web console were not checked.
The exact INI section names for 'upnp.enabled' and the other dotted options were taken from the documentation table, not tested.

name: I2P (Java I2P router)
purpose: The reference Java implementation of the I2P anonymity network, with a router console, I2PTunnel, I2PSnark and a SAM bridge that is off by default.

platforms.other: Linux, macOS, OpenWrt and other Unix-like systems.

MSI property DO_NOT_LAUNCH suppresses the UI after installation.
platforms.other: Linux kernel module and wg-quick, macOS, iOS, Android, BSDs.

interfaces.description: wireguard.exe /installtunnelservice <path\name.conf> (creates service WireGuardTunnel$name), /uninstalltunnelservice <name>, /installmanagerservice, /uninstallmanagerservice, /dumplog [/tail], /update, /removedriver; wg.exe show/set for runtime inspection.
interfaces.authentication: Administrator rights for services; wg.exe on a .conf.dpapi tunnel needs Local System or Administrator

interfaces.description: wg-quick style .conf files ([Interface] PrivateKey, Address, DNS; [Peer] PublicKey, AllowedIPs, Endpoint, PersistentKeepalive); the manager service encrypts files dropped in %ProgramFiles%\WireGuard\Data\Configurations\ to .conf.dpapi.
Tray manager UI shown to built-in Administrators (a limited UI for Network Configuration Operators when enabled by registry).

remoteManagement: None on Windows beyond standard service management; the remote peer is typically a router or Linux server configured separately.
nodeCompatibility: Transparent to Bitcoin Core and Electrum clients: once the tunnel is up the remote node's RPC or Electrum port is reachable on its tunnel address. Core must then bind or allow that tunnel address explicitly (rpcbind/rpcallowip), which BTCortex should only do with explicit consent.
networking: UDP to the peer's Endpoint (default listen port chosen per configuration); creates a Wintun network adapter; AllowedIPs decides routing (0.0.0.0/0 routes all traffic through the peer).
security: Installation, tunnel services and driver need administrator rights, so the zero-touch rule cannot be met without one UAC approval. Private keys live in .conf or DPAPI-protected .conf.dpapi files. The peer operator (or VPN provider) sees all traffic metadata and, for full-tunnel configurations, all destinations: never label a WireGuard connection as anonymous. PreUp/PostUp scripts run only when an administrator enables a registry key.

integrationMechanisms: Generate X25519 key pairs and wg-quick configurations for a remote-node tunnel and show them for import, or install them with one explicit UAC elevation through /installtunnelservice
Detect installed tunnels (services named WireGuardTunnel$*) and the tunnel adapter's addresses to offer remote endpoints
Never present the tunnel as anonymous; mark connections as 'encrypted tunnel'

feasibility.notes: Well-documented CLI and service model, but every lifecycle step needs administrator rights.

name: Tailscale
purpose: WireGuard-based mesh VPN ('tailnet') with a hosted coordination server, NAT traversal and DERP relays; Serve publishes a local service inside the tailnet and Funnel publishes it on the public internet.

platforms.windowsVersions: Windows 10 or later, Windows Server 2016 or later
platforms.windowsDistribution: tailscale-setup-1.104.2.exe, tailscale-setup-full-1.104.2.exe and per-architecture MSIs (tailscale-setup-1.104.2-amd64.msi, -arm64.msi, -x86.msi); default INSTALLDIR C:\Program Files\Tailscale; MSI properties include TS_UNATTENDEDMODE, TS_LOGINURL and TS_NOLAUNCH.
platforms.other: Linux, macOS, iOS, Android, Synology, BSDs.

interfaces.description: tailscale.exe up, status [--json], ip, ping, serve <port> (tailnet-only HTTPS proxy), funnel <port> (public internet), cert, login --login-server <url>.
interfaces.authentication: Tailnet identity of the logged-in user or device

interfaces.description: Tray client; by default it runs only while the user is logged in unless 'Run unattended' is enabled.

cli: tailscale status --json; tailscale serve 3000; tailscale funnel 3000; tailscale cert <machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net; tailscale login --login-server https://headscale.example
remoteManagement: Hosted admin console and API (Tailscale) or a self-hosted Headscale server; BTCortex only reads local state through the CLI.
nodeCompatibility: Transparent: a remote node's RPC, Electrum or web ports become reachable on its tailnet address or MagicDNS name; Bitcoin Core must allow that address explicitly. Tailscale Serve can expose a loopback-bound web UI to the tailnet without changing its bind address.

dependencies.notes: Self-hosted replacement for Tailscale's coordination server.

networking: Outbound UDP (WireGuard) with NAT traversal; falls back to DERP relays over HTTPS; Funnel only on ports 443, 8443 and 10000 through Funnel relay servers, which proxy TCP without decrypting; HTTPS certificates from Let's Encrypt for <machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net.
security: Encrypted private network, not anonymity: the coordination server (Tailscale Inc. or Headscale) knows the devices, their keys and public IP addresses. Enabling HTTPS publishes machine names and the tailnet DNS name in Certificate Transparency logs ('Do not enable the HTTPS feature if any of your machine names contain sensitive information'). Serve is tailnet-only and adds identity headers, so the backend must listen on localhost. Funnel makes a service reachable by anyone with the URL; BTCortex must never use Funnel for node RPC, Electrum or Lightning management interfaces.
licenceNotes: tailscaled and the CLI are open source; the Windows GUI wrapper is not ('The GUI wrappers on non-open source platforms are themselves not open source').
integrationMechanisms: Detect the client (C:\Program Files\Tailscale\tailscale.exe) and read 'tailscale status --json' to list peers and addresses
Offer remote node endpoints on tailnet addresses
With explicit consent, run 'tailscale serve' for a loopback-bound BTCortex-managed web UI; never Funnel by default

feasibility.notes: Installation is a per-machine MSI and login is interactive; BTCortex should detect and use an existing installation rather than install it.

remoteManagement: The basis of BTCortex's remote management (specification section 26): command execution, service control, log retrieval and tunnels to remote RPC, Electrum and Tor control ports, with permissions separate from Bitcoin RPC credentials.
nodeCompatibility: Port forwarding lets BTCortex reach a remote node's loopback-bound RPC (8332), Electrum (50001/50002) or REST ports without changing their bind addresses.

Use key-based authentication with keys protected by DPAPI or an agent. Installing or enabling sshd on the Windows machine needs administrator rights and opens port 22 through a firewall rule; BTCortex should not do this by default.

integrationMechanisms: Use the in-box ssh.exe (or an embedded SSH library) for remote-host profiles with pinned host keys
Create local port forwards for remote RPC, Electrum and Tor control ports
Detect whether the client feature is present with Get-WindowsCapability or by probing the System32 path

name: Frigate Electrum Server
purpose: Electrum server for BIP 352 silent payments by Sparrow's author: indexes Taproot-era transactions from Bitcoin Core into DuckDB and scans server-side with ephemeral client keys, optionally GPU-accelerated; can proxy ordinary Electrum requests to a co-located Fulcrum or electrs.

platforms.windowsDistribution: frigate-1.6.1-win-x86_64.zip; frigate-1.6.1-manifest.txt (SHA-256) signed in frigate-1.6.1-manifest.txt.asc by Craig Raw's key D4D0 D320 2FC0 6849 A257 B38D E946 1833 4C67 4B40 (the same key as Sparrow).
platforms.other: Linux (.deb, .rpm, tar.gz for x86_64 and aarch64), macOS (.dmg for x86_64 and aarch64).

interfaces.description: Electrum protocol 1.3 to 1.6 plus the silent-payments extension (blockchain.silentpayments.subscribe); listeners configured as tcp://, ssl:// URLs (default tcp://0.0.0.0:50001 when nothing is set).
Loopback-only admin JSON-RPC port (adminPort, for example 50003) offering getinfo for health checks; frigate-cli.

%APPDATA%\Frigate\config.toml ([core] server, authType COOKIE or USERPASS, dataDir, zmqSequenceEndpoint; [index] startHeight, cacheSize; [scan] computeBackend, memoryLimit; [server] tcp, ssl, adminPort, backendElectrumServer; [limits]); DuckDB file db\frigate.duckdb.

cli: frigate [-n testnet|testnet4|signet|regtest] [-d <home directory>]; frigate-cli
nodeCompatibility: Bitcoin Core 28 or later (for Electrum protocol 1.6) with txindex=1, so it cannot run against a pruned node; cookie authentication by default; zmqpubsequence strongly recommended when a backend Electrum server is configured. Sparrow uses it for silent-payment wallets (Sparrow cannot scan silent payments through Bitcoin Core).

dependencies.notes: Backend Electrum server for non-silent-payment requests, on a different port.

networking: Occupies the canonical Electrum ports 50001/50002, so a co-located Fulcrum or electrs must move to another port; BTCortex must set tcp/ssl to 127.0.0.1 explicitly because the default listener binds all interfaces.
storage: About 18 GB for the DuckDB index (README, 2026), growing slowly; indexing starts at block 709,632 on mainnet.
resources: Indexing uses about 4 GB RAM for the default scriptPubKey cache (cacheSize 10M); DuckDB defaults to 80 % of system RAM; 16 GB is 'a comfortable baseline' and 8 GB works with a reduced cache and memoryLimit. Optional GPU (CUDA, Metal, OpenCL).
security: Server-side scanning means the server receives the wallet's scan private key (kept only in RAM); this is acceptable for a self-hosted instance but a public Frigate learns which payments belong to the user, so BTCortex should only connect wallets to the user's own instance. Releases are signed with a known key.
integrationMechanisms: Download the Windows ZIP, verify the manifest signature (Craig Raw key) and SHA-256, extract per user
Generate config.toml (Core cookie path, tcp on 127.0.0.1, adminPort, memoryLimit and cacheSize sized to the machine, backendElectrumServer when Fulcrum is present)
Health through the admin getinfo call and the 'Electrum server listening' log line
Configure Sparrow silent-payment wallets to use the local Frigate

feasibility.notes: Native Windows build with signed releases and a documented configuration; gated on an unpruned node with txindex, at least 8 GB RAM and about 18 GB of disk, so it is not possible on the 5.9 GB-RAM pruned test machine.

notes: Implements the 'Remote Scanner (Ephemeral)' model of the BIP352 Index Server Specification (work in progress).

sources.title: BIP352 Silent Payments Index Server Specification (WIP)

unverifiedClaims: Whether the Windows ZIP bundles its own Java runtime and how it is started on Windows (launcher path) were not checked.
GPU acceleration on Windows was not tested.
